note: GLightbox Inline (submodule of glightbox) opens on-page elements, pages, videos, or images in a GLightbox popup when a link has the class 'glightbox-inline'. href = a CSS selector (#id), a path/URL (/node/42, https://...), or a media URL; optional data-glightbox sets modal size. It attaches its library on every page via hook_page_attachments; no config, permissions, or Drush. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the class contract (content whose body uses a glightbox-inline link) and the module's enabled state.

evals.prompt: With the glightbox_inline module enabled, how do I make a link open an element that is already on the page (e.g. a hidden div with id 'signup') inside a GLightbox popup?
evals.expected_output: Add the class 'glightbox-inline' to the link and set its href to the element's selector, e.g. Open. GLightbox opens the first element matching that selector in the modal.

evals.prompt: Using glightbox_inline, how do I open a whole page (like /node/42) or a video URL inside the lightbox instead of an on-page element? How do I control the popup size?
evals.expected_output: Give the glightbox-inline link an href that is a path or URL (e.g. href="/node/42", or a YouTube/MP4 URL) and it loads that page/video in the modal (content can also load via AJAX). Control the modal size with data-glightbox, e.g. data-glightbox="width: 700; height: auto".

evals.prompt: What does the glightbox_inline module require to work, and does it have any configuration options?
evals.expected_output: It requires the main GLightbox module (which needs the GLightbox JS library in /libraries). It has no configuration, permissions, or Drush; enabling it and adding the glightbox-inline class is the whole setup. It attaches its library on every page via hook_page_attachments.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a published Article whose body uses glightbox_inline to open on-page content in a popup. Inspect the content and state the CSS class that triggers the inline GLightbox.
evals.expected_output: The trigger class is glightbox-inline. The Article 'glb inline demo' body contains <a class="glightbox-inline" href="#glb-target">, which opens the on-page #glb-target element in the lightbox.

evals.prompt: Is the glightbox_inline module currently enabled on this Drupal site? Inspect the running site to answer.
evals.expected_output: Yes, glightbox_inline is enabled (e.g. drush pm:list --status=enabled includes glightbox_inline, or \Drupal::moduleHandler()->moduleExists('glightbox_inline') is TRUE).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (with glightbox_inline enabled), create a published Article titled exactly 'GLB Inline Panel' whose body contains a link that, when clicked, opens an on-page element in a GLightbox popup using the glightbox_inline feature. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An Article titled 'GLB Inline Panel' exists whose body has a link with class "glightbox-inline" and an href pointing at an on-page selector (e.g. href="#panel"). That is the glightbox_inline contract for opening an on-page element.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (with glightbox_inline enabled), create a published Article titled exactly 'GLB Inline Page' whose body has a link that loads a page/URL inside a GLightbox popup using the glightbox_inline feature (e.g. loading /node/1 in the modal). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An Article titled 'GLB Inline Page' exists whose body has a link with class "glightbox-inline" whose href is a path or URL (starts with / or http), which glightbox_inline loads into the modal.
